separable: no object — *ice over* is intransitive, and the surface is the subject: *the pond iced over*. ✗ *iced over the pond*.
gloss: To become covered with a layer of ice.
examples: The pond *iced over* during the cold snap.
Our windshield *ices over* almost every night in January.
By morning the steps had *iced over* and nobody could get down them.

separable: no object — *ice up* is intransitive: *the lock iced up*, never ✗ *the cold iced up the lock*.
gloss: To get clogged or coated with ice so that something stops working.
examples: The wings *iced up* on the way over the mountains.
If the gutters *ice up*, the water backs into the roof.
The lock had *iced up* and the key would not turn.

separable: inseparable — *with* never lets go of its object: *I identify with her*, *I identify with them*, never ✗ *I identify her with*.
gloss: To feel that you understand and share another person's feelings or situation.
examples: I really *identified with* the older sister in the movie.
Kids *identify with* characters their own age.
She says she has never been able to *identify with* her father.

separable: the object comes before *with*: *identify the smell with childhood*, *identify it with childhood*. *With* still keeps its own object: ✗ *identify the smell childhood with*.
gloss: To connect one thing with another in your mind, or to be publicly connected with something.
examples: Most Americans *identify* that accent *with* the South.
He has been *identified with* the reform movement for years.
Don't *identify* the brand too closely *with* one celebrity.

separable: separable — *idle away the afternoon*, and *idle the afternoon away*. With a pronoun the split is required: *idled it away*, never ✗ *idled away it*.
gloss: To spend time doing nothing in particular, in a way that wastes it.
examples: We *idled away* the whole afternoon on the porch.
He *idles away* his mornings watching the river.
I have *idled* half the summer *away* and have nothing to show for it.

separable: inseparable — the object stays after *on*: *improve on her time*, *improve on it*, never ✗ *improve it on*. *Improve upon* is the formal variant.
gloss: To do or make something better than what came before.
examples: Nobody has *improved on* that record in twenty years.
The new version *improves on* the old one in every way.
She keeps *improving on* her own best time.

separable: inseparable — the person follows *on*: *impressed on the kids*, never ✗ *impressed the kids on*. What you want understood goes in front of *on* or in a *how / that* clause. *Impress upon* is the formal variant.
gloss: To make someone understand clearly how important something is.
examples: My mother *impressed on* us that we should always call.
The coach *impresses* the rules *on* every new player.
He had *impressed on* her how little time was left.

separable: no object — *inch along* is intransitive: *traffic inched along*. ✗ *inched the car along*.
gloss: To move forward very slowly, a little at a time.
examples: Traffic *inched along* for an hour.
The line *inches along* about one person a minute.
We were *inching along* in second gear the whole way.
contrast: *Inch* ends in *-ch*, so the third person adds *-es*: *inches along*.

separable: no object — the thing that rises is the subject: *prices inched up*, never ✗ *they inched up prices*.
gloss: To rise slowly, by small amounts.
examples: Gas prices *inched up* again last week.
Her temperature has been *inching up* all night.
Support for the measure *inches up* every time somebody explains it.

ru: позволять себе, позволить себе; предаваться, предаться
separable: inseparable — what you allow yourself follows *in*: *indulge in dessert*, *indulge in it*, never ✗ *indulge it in*.
gloss: To let yourself have or do something enjoyable that you usually hold back from.
examples: Once a week we *indulge in* takeout.
He *indulged in* a second piece of cake.
She has been *indulging in* long baths since the baby started sleeping.

separable: inseparable — the person you report follows *on*: *inform on his partner*, *inform on him*, never ✗ *inform him on*.
gloss: To tell the police or an authority about something someone has done wrong.
examples: He *informed on* his own partner to get a lighter sentence.
Two employees have *informed on* the manager.
Nobody in the neighborhood was *informing on* anybody.

separable: inseparable — *into* holds its object: *inquire into the delay*, *inquire into it*, never ✗ *inquire it into*.
gloss: To investigate something officially in order to find out the facts.
examples: A committee is *inquiring into* the delays.
The state *inquired into* how the money was spent.
Two agencies have *inquired into* the same contract.

separable: inseparable — *on* keeps its object: *intrude on their evening*, *intrude on them*, never ✗ *intrude them on*. *Intrude upon* is the formal variant.
gloss: To interrupt or disturb someone's private time or space when you are not wanted.
examples: I don't want to *intrude on* your evening.
Reporters *intruded on* the family for weeks.
Work keeps *intruding on* what is left of the weekend.

ru: звать с собой, позвать с собой
separable: separable — *invite your brother along*, and with a pronoun the object must sit in the middle: *invite him along*, never ✗ *invite along him*.
gloss: To ask someone to come with you to something you are already going to.
examples: Can I *invite* my brother *along*?
They *invited* us *along* to the game.
She is *inviting* a few people *along* for the drive.

separable: separable — *invited the neighbors in* or *invited in the neighbors*, but a pronoun must split the pair: *invited us in*, never ✗ *invited in us*.
gloss: To ask someone standing outside to come into your home or office.
examples: She opened the door and *invited* us *in*.
He *invites* the mail carrier *in* for coffee every winter.
They were *invited in* and given a seat by the fire.

separable: separable — *invite out the whole team*, *invite the whole team out*, and with a pronoun always *invite her out*, never ✗ *invite out her*.
gloss: To ask someone to go somewhere with you, especially on a date.
examples: He finally *invited* her *out*.
I am *inviting* the whole team *out* for pizza.
She has been *invited out* twice this week.

ru: приглашать в гости, пригласить в гости
separable: separable — *invite the Nelsons over* or *invite over the Nelsons*, and with a pronoun always *invite them over*, never ✗ *invite over them*.
gloss: To ask someone to come to your home.
examples: Let's *invite* the Nelsons *over* on Saturday.
They *invited* us *over* for dinner twice last month.
She is *inviting* a few friends *over* to watch the game.

separable: separable — *iron out the details*, *iron the details out*, and with a pronoun always *iron them out*, never ✗ *iron out them*.
gloss: To settle the small problems or disagreements that are left in something.
examples: The lawyers still have to *iron out* a few details.
We *ironed out* our differences over lunch.
Once the schedule is *ironed out*, I will send it around.

separable: inseparable — what you want follows *for*: *itching for a fight*, *itching for it*, never ✗ *itch it for*. Usually in the *-ing* form.
gloss: To want something very badly and be impatient to get it.
examples: He has been *itching for* a fight all week.
By August the whole town *itches for* one cool morning.
The team *itched for* a rematch all season.
contrast: *Itch* ends in *-tch*, so the third person adds *-es*: *itches for*.

separable: separable — *jack up the price*, *jack the price up*, and with a pronoun always *jack it up*, never ✗ *jack up it*.
gloss: To raise a price, rate, or amount sharply; informal.
examples: The hotels *jack up* their rates during the festival.
They *jacked* the rent *up* two hundred dollars.
Premiums are being *jacked up* again this year.

separable: separable when it takes an object — *jammed up the printer*, *jammed the printer up*, *jammed it up* — but just as often there is no object at all: *the freeway jams up*.
transitivity: both — transitive (*a wet sheet jammed up the printer*), intransitive (*the freeway jams up at five*)
gloss: To become blocked or stuck, or to make something blocked or stuck.
examples: The freeway *jams up* every day at five.
A wet sheet of paper *jammed up* the printer.
Downtown has been *jamming up* since the bridge closed.

separable: separable — *jazz up the report*, *jazz the report up*, and with a pronoun always *jazz it up*, never ✗ *jazz up it*.
gloss: To make something more lively, colorful, or interesting; informal.
examples: A few photos would *jazz up* the report.
She *jazzed* the plain cake *up* with berries.
They are *jazzing up* the lobby before the opening.

separable: separable, and the object almost always sits in the middle: *jerk me around*, *jerking the customers around*. ✗ *jerk around me*.
gloss: To waste someone's time or treat them unfairly by not being straight with them; informal.
examples: The airline *jerked* us *around* for three days.
Stop *jerking* me *around* and tell me the price.
He felt he had been *jerked around* by the whole department.

separable: inseparable — *with* keeps its object: *jibe with the facts*, *jibe with them*, never ✗ *jibe them with*.
gloss: To agree with or match other information; American, and often spelled *jive with* in casual writing.
examples: His account doesn't *jibe with* the security footage.
Her numbers *jibed with* mine exactly.
Nothing he said was *jibing with* what we had been told.

separable: usually no object at all — *everybody joined in*. When the activity is named, *in* holds it and cannot be split: *join in the song*, never ✗ *join the song in*.
transitivity: both — intransitive (*we all joined in*), transitive with *in* (*she joined in the conversation*)
gloss: To start taking part in an activity that other people have already started.
examples: By the second verse everybody had *joined in*.
She *joins in* every discussion.
The kids were shy at first, but they are *joining in* now.

ru: вступать в армию, вступить в армию
separable: no object — *join up* is intransitive: *he joined up at eighteen*. ✗ *joined up the army*.
gloss: To enlist in the armed forces.
examples: His grandfather *joined up* at eighteen.
Two of my cousins are *joining up* in the fall.
Plenty of people *join up* for the training alone.

separable: inseparable — the three words stay together and the other party follows *with*: *join up with them*, never ✗ *join them up with*.
gloss: To meet other people and go on together, or to team up with them.
examples: We will *join up with* the others at the trailhead.
Two small firms *joined up with* a national chain.
She is *joining up with* her sister in Denver.

separable: no object at all — *joke around* is intransitive: *they were joking around*. ✗ *joke him around*.
gloss: To behave in a silly, playful way, saying things you do not mean seriously.
examples: The two of them *joke around* all through practice.
We were just *joking around* — nobody meant it.
He has *joked around* so much that nobody takes his warnings seriously.

separable: separable — *jot down the address*, *jot the address down*, and with a pronoun always *jot it down*, never ✗ *jot down it*.
gloss: To write something down quickly and informally, so you do not forget it.
examples: Let me *jot down* your number.
She *jotted* the address *down* on a napkin.
I have been *jotting down* ideas all week.

separable: separable — *juice up the engine*, *juice the engine up*, and with a pronoun always *juice it up*, never ✗ *juice up it*.
gloss: To make something more powerful or more exciting; informal.
examples: The new coach has *juiced up* the offense.
Producers *juiced* the trailer *up* with extra explosions.
They are *juicing up* the engine for the race.

separable: separable — *jumble up the letters*, *jumble the letters up*, *jumble them up*. Most often heard in the passive: *everything got jumbled up*.
gloss: To mix things together into a disordered mess.
examples: The move *jumbled up* all our boxes.
Somebody had *jumbled* the files *up*.
Stop *jumbling up* the dates — I cannot follow you.

separable: inseparable — *at* keeps its object: *jump at the chance*, *jump at it*, never ✗ *jump it at*.
gloss: To accept an offer or a chance eagerly and without hesitating.
examples: She *jumped at* the chance to go to Tokyo.
Most students *jump at* free food.
I would have *jumped at* an offer like that.

separable: no object — *jump in* is intransitive: *feel free to jump in*. What you jump into needs *into*: *jumped into the argument*.
gloss: To join a conversation or an activity suddenly, without waiting to be asked.
examples: Feel free to *jump in* if I get something wrong.
She *jumped in* before he could finish the sentence.
Two other people were *jumping in* with questions.

separable: inseparable — the person criticized follows *on*: *jumped on him*, never ✗ *jumped him on*.
gloss: To criticize or attack someone quickly and harshly for something they said or did.
examples: Don't *jump on* me — I am only asking.
The press *jumped on* one line in the speech.
He gets *jumped on* every time he raises the subject.

ru: не упускать, не упустить (возможность); быстро хвататься
separable: inseparable — what you act on follows *on*: *jump on the offer*, *jump on it*, never ✗ *jump it on*.
gloss: To act on an opportunity immediately, before it is gone.
examples: Good apartments go fast, so *jump on* it.
They *jumped on* the discount the minute it appeared.
Every studio is *jumping on* the new format.

ru: бросаться в глаза, броситься в глаза
separable: inseparable — the three words stay in order and the person follows *at*: *jumped out at me*, never ✗ *jumped me out at*.
gloss: To be so noticeable that someone sees it right away.
examples: One number *jumped out at* me right away.
Nothing in the report *jumps out at* you as wrong.
The typo in the headline was *jumping out at* everyone.
